titleEn: Stop! Check the Water! One Stone at a Time!

pages.text: "I'll go first!" Quick-handed monkey Taro ran to the stream. The overnight rain had stopped that morning. Water rushed loudly past.
"Let's go to the shore! It's just across the stream." Taro put a foot on the first stepping stone. "Why count stones? I'll just jump!"
As he got ready to jump, Mumu bounded in front of him. "Stop!" Taro froze with one foot raised.
Mumu pointed to the middle of the stream. One stone was underwater—the one where the toad had sat yesterday. "The night's rain raised the water."
Mumu listened at the bank. The rushing was much louder than yesterday. "A louder sound means stronger water. Not yet."

"Then how do we cross?" Taro asked. "One, stop before the stream! Two, check the water and look for covered stones! Three, hold a grown-up's hand and cross one stone at a time!" Taro repeated, "Stop! Check the Water! One Stone at a Time!"
They did not cross and went back the way they had come. From the porch, they listened to the rushing water. It went on until evening.
The next morning, the water had dropped. The toad sat on its stone again. Holding Mom's hand, Taro counted the stones and crossed carefully. Now he stood on the middle stone beside the toad.

Hop! He reached the shore across the stream and tapped twice with his branch. "One, stop! Two, check the water! Three, hold a grown-up's hand, one stone at a time!" Now Taro stopped first at the stream.

Mumu held his hand tightly. "Thank you for waiting instead of jumping." The more hurried they were, the more they needed to check the water before crossing. Together, they called, "Stop! Check the Water! One Stone at a Time!"
